title: Choose the visual world for Saans
question: Structure is settled: guided setup, then a Today timeline. The roll assigned the Route Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Route Board
options.lineage: Delhi bus-stop route boards and bilingual transit signage
options.thesis: The day is a bus route: each hour a stop, every label Hindi over English, the AQI a route number.
options.viewport: Green board header with the AQI as an orange route number, then the day as stops on a vertical line.
options.risk: Bilingual stacking can crowd small screens if every label is doubled.

raised.raise: One current stop owns the focus at full size with the next stop already peeking below it.
Before and after are drawn on one shared scale and baseline so the gain is read, not told.
Tapping an hour pulls its numbers into focus while the rest of the day quiets.

options.label: Panchang Bands
options.lineage: the Hindi wall-calendar panchang and its choghadiya hour table
options.thesis: The day divided into named hour bands, read like the almanac every Indian home already checks.
options.viewport: Today's headline, then an eight-band hour table coloured stay in, careful, best.
options.risk: Warm paper with a red-orange accent is also the default look of this whole category.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: a 1971 pocket airline timetable under tinted glass slides
options.thesis: The day as a rack of slides along one hour rail, rank carried by weight and case, never size.
options.viewport: An hour tick rail over a raked rack of slides, each stating its own heading and a filled or hollow mark.
options.case: Holds product clarity because hours are its native unit; loses on audience identification, an airline timetable is not Delhi's.
options.risk: Sheared containers and one type size strain Hindi script on a phone.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.viewport: One item fills the screen with a right rail of actions.
options.case: Loses both axes: swipe-per-item hides the day's whole shape and feels like entertainment, not a health decision.
options.kept: One thing owns the screen and the next is already waiting.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.viewport: Side A and side B tracklists ruled in ballpoint.
options.case: Loses both axes: handwriting reads as nostalgia and weakens trust in health numbers.
options.kept: Two halves that must each fit the whole: the day split cleanly into daytime and night.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.viewport: A headline built from visible pixels over dense columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: coarse pixel type is hard to read in Devanagari and says design school, not family care.
options.kept: Total commitment of a single display voice.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: a botanical folio following one plant through a year
options.viewport: Five plates on one shared stem and baseline.
options.case: Loses both axes: cream-and-engraving is calm but says garden, not urgent winter air.
options.kept: Registered comparison: same scale and ground so change reads honestly.

options.label: Datamatics
options.lineage: black-and-white barcode and sine-lattice data art
options.viewport: A wall of hairline bars with dense numerals.
options.case: Loses both axes: strobing monochrome alarms a family and drops the colour the AQI scale depends on.
options.kept: Selecting a column pulls its numbers into focus while the rest quiets.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean mobile air-quality app: AQI ring, forecast and tips as white cards.
canonCard.viewport: An AQI ring with a category tag, then a stack of tip cards and tab bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other AQI app, and it can't show the day's timeline.
